comparison: Perfect agreement on ratio comparisons (C43-C45). Both evaluations find these quantitative findings well-supported by Figure 3 data showing differential binocular combination rules across pathways.

Both address modeling results (C59-C64, C100), but with different conclusions. OpenEval finds the model well-supported and appropriate, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about model limitations, particularly whether it can predict intermodulation responses with the fitted parameters.

Strong agreement on matching experiment results (C4, C55-C58). Both evaluations find the psychophysical data well-supported and consistent with cortical processing patterns, with peer reviewers noting the behavioral measure as a strength.

Significant disagreement on intermodulation findings (C93-C96). OpenEval finds the IM results clearly supported and consistent with nonlinearity claims, while peer reviewers express fundamental uncertainty about reconciling IM presence with claims of largely linear/monocular processing.

Both rate mechanistic interpretations (C5-C6, C77, C82) as uncertain. OpenEval notes the interpretation is speculative with alternative architectures not ruled out; peer reviewers acknowledge solid evidence for differences but express uncertainty about broader theoretical interpretation and generalizability.

Strong agreement on pupillometry results (C2-C3, C23, C27-C35). Both find the subcortical pathway findings well-supported with solid evidence. Peer reviewers also accept related modeling parameters (C45, C60-C61, C63, C66) as demonstrating pathway-specific differences.

Significant disagreement on EEG findings (C36-C42). OpenEval finds the cortical results well-supported with reasonable inference about linear processing, while peer reviewers express fundamental uncertainty about reconciling claims of 'largely monocular' processing with robust intermodulation components.

Both address alternative monocular channel interpretation (C90-C91) with uncertainty. OpenEval notes this speculation is not directly tested; peer reviewers directly challenge this interpretation given the intermodulation findings, noting the views are 'in striking contrast.'

Agreement on methodological approach and spectral signatures (C17-C22). OpenEval finds pupillometry results well-supported by spectral data; peer reviewers explicitly praise the frequency-tagging methodology as a strength and novel experimental design.

Agreement on literature context (C68-C69, C50). Both evaluations accept the comparison to prior work on gratings as appropriate and well-supported, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming the flicker results differ markedly from grating studies.

Agreement on frequency-dependence findings (C50-C54). OpenEval finds the replication across frequencies well-supported; peer reviewers confirm the key comparison showing flicker differs from gratings, validating the novelty of the findings.

Partial agreement on modeling utility (C100). OpenEval finds the common model architecture successfully supports quantitative comparisons; peer reviewers acknowledge modeling as a strength but raise concerns about limitations in making joint predictions across conditions.

Disagreement on summary conclusions (C65, C99). OpenEval finds these well-supported by convergent evidence; peer reviewers express uncertainty about the linear processing interpretation (C65) given intermodulation findings, though they accept the comparison to spatial pattern vision (C99).

Both address broader theoretical claims (C98) with different emphasis. OpenEval finds summary conclusions well-supported; peer reviewers acknowledge solid evidence but note questions remain about how findings relate to extant literature and broader vision science interests.

Agreement on perception following cortical rules (C67). OpenEval finds this conclusion well-supported by convergent evidence; peer reviewers implicitly accept this through their support of the matching experiment as confirmatory evidence.

OpenEval evaluates functional interpretations (C78-C81) as uncertain and speculative without direct testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific evolutionary/functional arguments.
OpenEval finds pupil-cortex interaction assumptions (C83-C85) appropriately acknowledged and justified. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological assumptions.
OpenEval finds the peripheral vision replication claim (C49) supported by appendix data, strengthening generalizability. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval finds all methodological claims (C101-C124) well-documented and appropriate, including sample sizes, analysis methods, and preregistration. No corresponding detailed peer review evaluation of these specific methodological elements.

OpenEval finds background claims (C1, C7-C18) appropriately supported by established literature. Peer reviewers address some methodological justification (C17-C18) but do not systematically evaluate all background claims.

OpenEval finds the methodological principle about intermodulation (C92) well-established and appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific theoretical foundation.
